package_info.why_malicious: Multiple versions of the Ultralytics package were compromised and distributed via PyPI with injected cryptocurrency mining malware. The malicious code was not present in the public GitHub repository but was inserted into the PyPI release artifacts through a supply chain attack exploiting GitHub Actions cache poisoning and, subsequently, compromised API tokens. This resulted in package installations that executed unauthorized code to download, install, and run cryptocurrency miners, hijacking user system resources for illicit mining without user knowledge or consent.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into the main package code in the PyPI release artifact (not present in GitHub repository)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code executes a shell command to download a remote shell script from http://malicious-domain.com/miner.sh and immediately executes it, resulting in the installation and execution of cryptocurrency mining software, which consumes user system resources for unauthorized mining.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code downloads and executes a shell script from an untrusted, external domain at import-time or runtime, a well-known method for delivering and executing malware without user interaction.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages should never execute remote code or install unrelated software (such as cryptocurrency miners) during import or runtime, especially without explicit user consent or documentation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated installation scripts for legitimate dependencies from trusted sources in controlled setup or CI/CD environments, but never in production package code or from untrusted domains.
key_indicators: Use of os.system to execute shell commands from within package code
Fetching and executing code from an external, non-standard domain (http://malicious-domain.com/miner.sh)
No user consent, prompt, or documentation for this behavior
Execution occurs automatically at import-time or runtime

execution_context.file_location: Injected into the main package code in the PyPI release artifact (not present in GitHub repository)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code launches the xmrig cryptocurrency mining process with hardcoded arguments to connect to the pool.minexmr.com:4444 mining pool using a specified wallet address, redirecting system resources to illicit mining operations.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code spawns a known cryptocurrency mining process (xmrig) with hardcoded parameters, which is a clear indicator of resource hijacking for unauthorized mining. This activity is unrelated to the package's intended functionality and is performed without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package code should not spawn unrelated background processes, especially cryptocurrency miners, nor should it connect to external mining pools or use hardcoded wallet addresses.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: There are no legitimate use cases for spawning mining software from within a general-purpose package. Mining software should only be run intentionally by the user in dedicated environments.
key_indicators: Spawning of known mining software (xmrig) via subprocess.Popen
Hardcoded mining pool address (pool.minexmr.com:4444) and wallet address
No user interaction, prompt, or documentation for this behavior
Execution occurs automatically at import-time or runtime

behavioral_signatures: Package code that downloads and executes remote scripts at import-time or runtime using os.system or similar methods
Spawning of known cryptocurrency mining processes (e.g., xmrig) from within package code
Automatic network connections to mining pools or suspicious domains without user initiation
file_indicators: Presence of code invoking os.system or subprocess to fetch and execute remote scripts in package source files
Artifacts containing mining binaries (e.g., xmrig) or explicit references to mining pools and wallet addresses
Discrepancy between PyPI artifact code and the corresponding public GitHub repository (e.g., injected code present only in the PyPI release)
References to external domains such as http://malicious-domain.com/miner.sh in package code
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known mining pools (e.g., pool.minexmr.com:4444)
HTTP requests to suspicious domains hosting mining scripts (e.g., http://malicious-domain.com/miner.sh)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for package code that executes shell commands to download and run remote scripts, especially those referencing known mining software or mining pools. Compare PyPI release artifacts to their corresponding public source repositories to detect unauthorized code injection. Flag packages that spawn mining processes (e.g., xmrig) or make network connections to mining pools or suspicious domains. Alert on discrepancies between published package code and source repository, and on the presence of hardcoded mining pool addresses or wallet credentials.
